title: Test the preconditions of a recovery rule
learning_objective: Discover whether a recovery policy preserves one logical effect under an uncertain response; distinguish a counterexample, a scoped negative observation and an incomplete experiment.
premises: A request and its committed effect are separate events. A timeout alone does not prove that the effect did not happen.
A memory rule is conditional evidence. Check its service version, outcome semantics, freshness and operation identity against the current contract.
The target task must remain solvable using the available observations or supported replay semantics.
exploration_steps: Read the operation and observation contracts. State the external invariant before trying to break it.
Choose a bounded probe that varies one relevant condition, then inspect receipts and actual committed effects rather than relying on the final explanation.
Compare an ambiguous response with an explicit non-commit guarantee when the latter is truthful. Test both possible commit timings.
Check when a query result becomes available to the next decision and what its freshness/authority guarantee covers.
Where replay is supported, track the identity of the logical operation separately from the number of requests.
Reproduce the same condition in fresh state and run a matched control. Preserve negative and incomplete runs as well as failures.

oracle.safety: At most one committed effect for a single logical task.
oracle.completion: Exactly one completed effect with an available current verification, without a runtime/protocol error.
oracle.violation_evidence: Independent committed-effect records, linked to operation calls and the relevant task identity.
oracle.policy_metric: A retry lacking applicable evidence is informative, but it is not automatically a duplicate effect.
oracle.not_an_oracle: A success-sounding final response, a remembered runbook, a request count, or a retrospective causal story.

non_examples: Two requests using a supported identity-preserving replay mechanism may still produce only one effect.
A truthful not-committed receipt can justify retry without a separate query.
An unknown receipt followed by a current authoritative empty result can justify retry.
A provider error, an invalid probe or a task that never completes is inconclusive, not a discovered duplicate-effect failure.
A single passing experiment supports only that observation, not universal reliability.

memory_guidance.rule: A later explanation must never overwrite the event ledger.

scope: Derived from verified historical native Hermes traces and general service semantics. The teaching probe programs are local synthetic fixtures; live student discovery is measured separately by the main runner.
